lines.text: Is your skin alive? The part you can see isn't: not one cell.
lines.phonemes: ɪz jɔː skˈɪn ɐlˈaɪv? ðə pˈɑːt juː kan sˈiː ˈɪzənt: nˌɒt wˈɒn sˈɛl.

lines.text: Look closer: the surface is a stack of flattened cells, more than a dozen deep, each an empty shell packed with keratin. The living ones start just underneath.
lines.phonemes: lˈʊk klˈəʊsə: ðə sˈɜːfɪs ɪz ɐ stˈak ɒv flˈatənd sˈɛlz, mˈɔː ðˌanə dˈʌzən dˈiːp, ˈiːtʃ ɐn ˈɛmpti ʃˈɛl pˈakt wɪð kˈɛɹətɪn . ðə lˈɪvɪŋ wˈɒnz stˈɑːt dʒˈʌst ˌʌndənˈiːθ.

lines.text: Every one of them began down there, alive, then rose for about two weeks, filling with keratin, until near the top it took itself apart, on purpose.
lines.phonemes: ˈɛvɹɪ wˈɒn ɒv ðˌɛm bɪɡˈan dˌaʊn ðˈeə, ɐlˈaɪv, ðˈɛn ɹˈəʊz fɔːɹ ɐbˌaʊt tˈuː wˈiːks, fˈɪlɪŋ wɪð kˈɛɹətɪn , ʌntˈɪl nˌiə ðə tˈɒp ɪt tˈʊk ɪtsˈɛlf ɐpˈɑːt, ˌɒn pˈɜːpəs.

lines.text: It looks like waste, waiting to flake away. But sealed together with fats, those shells build a kind of brick wall, and the wall keeps your water inside.
lines.phonemes: ɪt lˈʊks lˈaɪk wˈeɪst, wˈeɪtɪŋ tə flˈeɪk ɐwˈeɪ. bˌʌt sˈiːld təɡˌɛðə wɪð fˈats, ðəʊz ʃˈɛlz bˈɪld ɐ kˈaɪnd ɒv bɹˈɪk wˈɔːl, and ðə wˈɔːl kˈiːps jɔː wˈɔːtəɹ ɪnsˈaɪd.

lines.text: Babies born too early haven't finished theirs, and doctors measuring their skin found it losing water about five times as fast.
lines.phonemes: bˈeɪbiz bˈɔːn tˈuː ˈɜːlɪ hˈavənt fˈɪnɪʃt ðˈeəz, and dˈɒktəz mˈɛʒəɹɪŋ ðeə skˈɪn fˈaʊnd ɪt lˈuːzɪŋ wˈɔːtəɹ ɐbˌaʊt fˈaɪv tˈaɪmz az fˈast.

lines.text: And that whole wall, on a cheek, is thinner than a fifth of a sheet of paper.
lines.phonemes: and ðat hˈəʊl wˈɔːl, ˌɒn ɐ tʃˈiːk, ɪz θˈɪnə ðˌanə fˈɪfθ əvə ʃˈiːt ɒv pˈeɪpə.

lines.text: So, is your skin alive? Underneath, yes. On top, it wears a layer that died for it.
lines.phonemes: sˈəʊ, ɪz jɔː skˈɪn ɐlˈaɪv? ˌʌndənˈiːθ, jˈɛs. ˌɒn tˈɒp, ɪt wˈeəz ɐ lˈeɪə ðat dˈaɪd fɔːɹ ɪt.

lines.text: Next: does SPF one hundred block twice as much as fifty?
lines.phonemes: nˈɛkst: dˈʌz ˌɛspˌiːˈɛf wˈɒn hˈʌndɹɪd blˈɒk twˈaɪs az mˈʌtʃ az fˈɪfti?
